summary.text: Ed Markey is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator from Massachusetts, elected in a June 2013 special election after 37 years in the U.S. House. A lawyer and former state legislator, he has served on the Senate Commerce, Environment and Public Works, HELP and Small Business committees.
He is seeking a third full term after defeating Rep. Seth Moulton in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary.

paragraphs.text: Markey was born in Malden, Massachusetts, on July 11, 1946, the son of a milkman, and attended Malden Catholic High School.
He earned a B.A. from Boston College in 1968 and a J.D. from Boston College Law School in 1972, and served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 1968 to 1973.
Markey worked as a lawyer and was elected to the Massachusetts House of Representatives, where he served two terms, from 1973 to 1976, representing Malden and Melrose.
He won a 1976 special election to the U.S. House, then the 7th District and later the 5th, and served until 2013, becoming Dean of the Massachusetts delegation.

In the House he chaired the Select Committee on Energy Independence and Global Warming from 2007 to 2010 and, for 20 years, chaired or was ranking member of the Subcommittee on Telecommunications and the Internet.

According to his Senate biography, he was the House author of the 1992 Cable Act and the Children's Online Privacy and Protection Act and co-authored the 2009 Waxman-Markey climate bill, which passed the House.

Markey won the Democratic primary on April 30, 2013, over Rep. Stephen Lynch, and the June 25, 2013 special election over Republican Gabriel Gomez, 54.9% to 44.7%, to fill the seat vacated by John Kerry.
He was re-elected in 2014 and in 2020, when he defeated Rep. Joe Kennedy III in the Democratic primary, 55.4% to 44.5%.

In the Senate he serves on the Commerce, Science, and Transportation; Environment and Public Works; Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions; and Small Business and Entrepreneurship committees, and is ranking member of the Small Business Committee and of the HELP subcommittee on Primary Health and Retirement Security.
He won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary against Moulton with 65.6% of the vote.
His Senate biography says he is married to Dr. Susan Blumenthal.
